{C.JOB_CAP}s are custom functions or procedures that {C.TIMESCALE_DB} runs on your schedule. The sections below show how to register one, test it, and change or remove it safely.

<Prerequisites context="procedure">
<PrereqCloudOrSelf />
</Prerequisites>

## Create a {C.JOB}

To create a {C.JOB}, create a [{C.PG} function](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/xfunc.html) or [procedure](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/xproc.html) that you want your database to execute, then set it up to run on a schedule.

<NumberedList>
<NumberedItem title="Define a function or procedure">
Wrap it in a `CREATE` statement:

```sql
CREATE FUNCTION <function_name> (job_id INT DEFAULT NULL, config JSONB DEFAULT NULL)
RETURNS VOID
DECLARE
    <declaration>;
BEGIN
    <function_body>;
END;
$<variable_name>$ LANGUAGE <language>;
```

For example, to create a function that reindexes a table within your database:

```sql
CREATE FUNCTION reindex_mytable(job_id INT DEFAULT NULL, config JSONB DEFAULT NULL)
RETURNS VOID
AS $$
BEGIN
   REINDEX TABLE mytable;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
```

`job_id` and `config` are required arguments in the function signature. This returns `CREATE FUNCTION` to indicate that the function has successfully been created.
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Call the function to validate">
```sql
select reindex_mytable();
```

The result looks like this:

```sql
 reindex_mytable
-----------------

(1 row)
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title={`Register your ${C.JOB} with \`add_job\``}>
Pass the name of your {C.JOB}, the schedule you want it to run on, and the content of your config. For the `config` value, if you don't need any special configuration parameters, set to `NULL`. For example, to run the `reindex_mytable` function every hour:

```sql
SELECT add_job('reindex_mytable', '1h', config => NULL);
```

The call returns a `job_id` and stores it along with `config` in the {C.TIMESCALE_DB} catalog.

The {C.JOB} runs on the schedule you set. You can also run it manually with [`run_job`](/reference/timescaledb/jobs-automation/run_job) passing `job_id`. When the {C.JOB} runs, `job_id` and `config` are passed as arguments.
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Validate the job">
List all currently registered {C.JOB}s with [`timescaledb_information.jobs`](/reference/timescaledb/informational-views/jobs):

```sql
SELECT * FROM timescaledb_information.jobs;
```

The result looks like this:

```sql
job_id |      application_name      | schedule_interval | max_runtime | max_retries | retry_period |      proc_schema      |    proc_name     |   owner   | scheduled |         config         |          next_start           | hypertable_schema | hypertable_name
--------+----------------------------+-------------------+-------------+-------------+--------------+-----------------------+------------------+-----------+-----------+------------------------+-------------------------------+-------------------+-----------------
1 | Telemetry Reporter [1]     | 24:00:00          | 00:01:40    |          -1 | 01:00:00     | _timescaledb_internal | policy_telemetry | postgres  | t         |                        | 2022-08-18 06:26:39.524065+00 |                   |
1000 | User-Defined Action [1000] | 01:00:00          | 00:00:00    |          -1 | 00:05:00     | public                | reindex_mytable  | tsdbadmin | t         |                        | 2022-08-17 07:17:24.831698+00 |                   |
(2 rows)
```
</NumberedItem>
</NumberedList>

## Test and debug a {C.JOB}

To debug a {C.JOB}, increase the log level and run the {C.JOB} manually with [`run_job`](/reference/timescaledb/jobs-automation/run_job) in the foreground. Because `run_job` is a stored procedure and not a function, run it with [`CALL`](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-call.html) instead of `SELECT`.

<NumberedList>
<NumberedItem title="Set the minimum log level to `DEBUG1`">
```sql
SET client_min_messages TO DEBUG1;
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title={`Run the ${C.JOB}`}>
Replace `1000` with your `job_id`:

```sql
CALL run_job(1000);
```
</NumberedItem>
</NumberedList>

## Alter and delete a {C.JOB}

Alter an existing {C.JOB} with [`alter_job`](/reference/timescaledb/jobs-automation/alter_job). You can change both the config and the schedule on which the {C.JOB} runs.

<NumberedList>
<NumberedItem title={`Change a ${C.JOB}'s config`}>
To replace the entire JSON config for a {C.JOB}, call `alter_job` with a new `config` object. For example, replace the JSON config for a {C.JOB} with ID `1000`:

```sql
SELECT alter_job(1000, config => '{"hypertable":"metrics"}');
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title={`Turn off ${C.JOB} scheduling`}>
To turn off automatic scheduling of a {C.JOB}, call `alter_job` and set `scheduled` to `false`. You can still run the {C.JOB} manually with `run_job`. For example, turn off the scheduling for a {C.JOB} with ID `1000`:

```sql
SELECT alter_job(1000, scheduled => false);
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Re-enable automatic scheduling">
To re-enable automatic scheduling of a {C.JOB}, call `alter_job` and set `scheduled` to `true`. For example, re-enable scheduling for a {C.JOB} with ID `1000`:

```sql
SELECT alter_job(1000, scheduled => true);
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title={`Delete a ${C.JOB} with \`delete_job\``}>
For example, to delete a {C.JOB} with ID `1000`:

```sql
SELECT delete_job(1000);
```
</NumberedItem>
</NumberedList>
